blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: A tsunami is caused by sudden displacement of ocean water resulting from underwater earthquakes, landslides, or volcanic eruptions.
In deep ocean water, tsunami waves can reach travel speeds exceeding 700 km/h.
Wave heights grow dramatically as the tsunami approaches coastal areas.
Rapid sea withdrawal is a characteristic phenomenon that often precedes the arrival of tsunami waves.

blocks.content: • Travel speeds may exceed 700 km/h in deep water.

items: Tsunami travel speeds in deep water can exceed 700 km/h.
Wave height increases dramatically near coastlines compared to deep water.
Rapid sea withdrawal along the coast serves as a crucial visual indicator of an impending tsunami.

blocks.content: • Wave height increases dramatically near coastlines.
• Often preceded by rapid sea withdrawal.
